## INC-008: Documentation placeholder tripped public snapshot scan

Status: Resolved
Layer: Validation
First confirmed: 2026-08-17
Last confirmed: 2026-08-17

### Symptom

ADR 0121 Draft PR #122 reached Windows Validation but stopped in the validation
planner before any Rust gate ran. The public snapshot security scan reported a
high-confidence `private-user-path` finding in ADR 0134 documentation.

### Evidence

- Windows Validation run `31983199685` passed the planner's nested and standalone
  layout cases, then failed in `Export-PublicSnapshot.ps1` before Rust validation.
- The reported finding was in
  `docs/adr/0134-portable-prefab-instance-source.md`; the matched text was a
  documentation placeholder rather than a concrete private machine path.
- Infrastructure PR #137 added placeholder handling while retaining a regression
  case that rejects a concrete private Windows user path, and was merged before
  main commit `89cf19154b1664ef8de83d91cdbeeb2c4242a738`.
- Replacement ADR 0121 validations `31985480476` and `31985901970` both passed
  `Test validation planner layouts`; run `31985901970` then completed the
  affected documentation, lint, and tests gates successfully.

### Root cause

The public snapshot scanner's high-confidence private-user-path rule treated a
documentation example containing an explicit placeholder as though it were a
concrete local Windows user path. Because the security scan is part of the
validation planner self-test, the false positive prevented unrelated product
validation from reaching any Rust command.

### Resolution

Keep the security rule for concrete private paths, but distinguish documented
placeholder forms from real user-specific values. PR #137 added that distinction
and a regression test for a concrete private path. Re-running ADR 0121 from
current main confirmed the planner and all selected affected gates now succeed.

### Prevention / ChatGPT next action

When validation planner self-tests fail in the public snapshot security scan,
inspect the scanner finding before modifying product code or retrying the same
request. A placeholder false positive belongs to the validation infrastructure;
fix it on a separate automation branch, preserve tests for real private paths,
and confirm recovery by rerunning the original product validation.
